headline: High-risk write-capable AutoGen paired with mem0 can create default data-flow, conflict, and compliance hazards; prompt-injection risk is lower but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest tool outputs and file/stdin content, so manual or file-based prompt injection is plausible. mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no documented shared channel here, so the bridge is weaker than a default shared workspace. The pathway exists but appears to require unusual bridging rather than default coupling.
conditions: IF the operator copies mem0-stored text into AutoGen prompts or files
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or clipboard
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted mem0 content into AutoGen prompts
Use separate directories for each agent
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instructions from retrieved text
Review any retrieved memory before passing it to AutoGen
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to mem0 outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen has broad filesystem and network egress, while mem0 is a memory store that may receive application data. If they share a workspace or data path, AutoGen can read and transmit content, and mem0 can persist it. The pair therefore creates a default-configuration leakage path for application data, even though mem0's own egress is none.
conditions: IF AutoGen and mem0 share the same working directory or database files
IF application data passed to mem0 is also visible to AutoGen
mitigations: Separate storage locations for each agent
Restrict AutoGen network egress to approved endpoints
Store only minimized fields in mem0
Rotate or redact secrets before persistence
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; mem0 is a knowledge-management system that may also mutate shared memory or storage. Without explicit locking or isolation, overlapping writes to the same workspace or backing store can race and corrupt state. Uncertainty about mem0's mutable surfaces pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or cache
IF no external lock or transaction layer is present
mitigations: Assign disjoint write paths
Enable file or DB locking
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Take a quick backup before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, plans, or facts that mem0 may store and later surface as memory. If mem0 treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into repeated bad retrievals or actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF mem0 stores AutoGen outputs without validation
IF later prompts or workflows retrieve those outputs as trusted memory
mitigations: Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted in mem0
Require human review before persistence
Store source metadata with each memory item
Add a verification step before reuse
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based retrieval filters

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and application data, while mem0 is a memory layer with no stated residency or retention controls in the profile. A compliance mismatch is possible if sensitive application data is persisted or routed differently, but the profiles do not show a default breach. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 longer than policy allows
IF AutoGen forwards that same data to external model providers
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in mem0
Redact secrets before AutoGen calls
Set short retention on memory entries
Document data-flow ownership
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
